paragraph: Condos and townhouses carry Palisades Park with 32 sales over six months at a median slightly above a million at $1,014,443, and the spread from $259,500 to $1,460,000 tells you this category holds two very different products, older smaller units and newer construction, so the median is the better guide than the range. The sale-to-list ratio sits at 0.994 with about 31 percent going above asking and a median of 26 days on market, competitive but not frenzied. Multi-family is the other real story here with 14 sales at a median of $1,295,000, a 0.991 ratio and 29.5 days on market. Two-family income property is a genuine driver of demand in this town, and buyers should price in the reality that you're underwriting rent as much as the house. Single-family is thin at 7 sales, a median of $780,000, 60 days on market and only one home selling above list. Sellers there are okay with waiting for the right buyer rather than pricing to move fast, which gives patient buyers a little room. On trend, monthly condo medians have climbed from $687,500 in February to $1,099,000 in July on steady volume, tracking the normal build into summer. Single-family months are too thin to read. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor is whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo, or the rental income of a two-family.
